title: Design Test Cases and Boundary Tests
learningObjectives: Design tests for typical, boundary and invalid input values
State expected results before executing each test case
Use assertions to check internal development-time assumptions
Test empty collections and minimum or maximum allowed values
Separate external input validation from optional assertions

understand.concept: A useful test suite covers typical inputs, boundaries, empty values and invalid cases. State expected results before running. Assertions check internal assumptions during development; explicit validation is still required for user input.
understand.whyItMatters: Boundary tests reveal off-by-one errors, missing validation and assumptions that ordinary examples do not expose. A planned test table makes expected behaviour explicit before implementation and supports repeatable regression checks.
understand.analogy: Testing a range is like checking both ends of a measuring scale as well as values in the middle. The endpoints often expose mistakes that a typical middle value cannot reveal.
understand.analogyLimit: A finite test set cannot prove a program correct for every possible input. Combine representative cases, boundaries, equivalence classes and risk-based tests.

explain.narrative:
## Design Test Cases and Boundary Tests

A useful test suite covers typical inputs, boundaries, empty values and invalid cases. State expected results before running. Assertions check internal assumptions during development; explicit validation is still required for user input.

## Build a boundary-value test set

For a valid percentage range of 0 through 100, test values immediately outside and on each boundary: -1, 0, 1, 99, 100 and 101. Add empty input, whitespace and non-numeric text when the value comes from a console or file.

## Keep expected results independent

Write the expected result before running the implementation. A test that calculates its expected value using the same faulty formula can repeat the defect. Name each case, record input and expected outcome, then compare actual output.

## Regression tests

When a defect is fixed, preserve the failing case as a test. Assertions are useful for internal invariants during development; validate external input explicitly because assertions may be disabled.

examples.title: Core concept
examples.code: public class Main { public static void main(String[] args) throws Exception { int input = 42; System.out.println(input > 0); } }
examples.explanation: Checks a typical positive value and confirms that it satisfies the greater-than-zero rule.

examples.title: Practical use
examples.code: public class Main { public static void main(String[] args) throws Exception { int input = 0; System.out.println(input >= 0); } }
examples.explanation: Checks the exact lower boundary at zero, which is accepted by this non-negative rule.

examples.title: Edge case
examples.code: public class Main { public static void main(String[] args) throws Exception { String input = ""; System.out.println(input.isBlank()); } }
examples.explanation: Checks an empty string as an edge case; isBlank returns true because it contains no visible characters.

examples.title: API behavior
examples.code: public class Main { public static void main(String[] args) throws Exception { int score = 105; System.out.println(score >= 0 && score <= 100); } }
examples.explanation: An invalid score outside the accepted range.

examples.title: Test and verify
examples.code: public class Main { public static void main(String[] args) throws Exception { int[] cases = {-1, 0, 100, 101}; for (int value : cases) System.out.println(value + " -> " + (value >= 0 && value <= 100)); } }
examples.explanation: Runs a small boundary test set and compares each result with the stated rule.

practise.guidedTask: Create a test table for a score validator with values -1, 0, 1, 99, 100 and 101. State expected results before coding.
practise.independentTask: Implement a method that accepts a percentage from 0 through 100. Add tests for minimum, maximum, empty input and malformed numeric text.
hints: Break the work into small methods with clear inputs and outputs.
Validate data before calculating or changing stored state.
Compile with JDK 21 and compare actual results with your test table.
practise.challenge: Add a regression test for every defect discovered. Explain why assertions are useful during development but cannot replace validation of user input.
